Command-Line Interface

clip.py exposes the core IFU Analyzer pipeline as a standalone CLI — useful for scripting, batch jobs, or headless server workflows where the GUI is not available.

  • Setup

  • Commands

  • auto-continuum — Automatic continuum detection and export

  • custom-continuum — Continuum from user-supplied points

  • subtract-continuum — Subtract a continuum from a spectrum

  • 2d-rotate — Rotate a 2D FITS image

  • 2d-contour — Extract contour coordinates from a 2D FITS image

  • Output Formats — quick reference

Setup

Run clip.py from the project root, one level above cube_explorer/:

python clip.py <command> [options]

Note

clip.py must be placed outside the cube_explorer/ folder so that the cube_explorer.data_loader import resolves correctly. If you see ImportError: Could not import CubeData, move clip.py one directory level up.

Commands

There are five CLI subcommands:

Command

Purpose

auto-continuum — Automatic continuum detection and export

Automatic continuum detection and export

custom-continuum — Continuum from user-supplied points

Continuum fit from user-supplied anchor points

subtract-continuum — Subtract a continuum from a spectrum

Subtract a continuum (constant, fitted curve, or anchor points)

2d-rotate — Rotate a 2D FITS image

Rotate a 2D FITS image with WCS update

2d-contour — Extract contour coordinates from a 2D FITS image

Extract contour coordinates from a 2D FITS image

auto-continuum — Automatic continuum detection and export

Automatically fits a continuum baseline to the cube’s integrated spectrum using median filtering, peak detection, and iterative sigma clipping, then saves the fitted curve as a text file.

python clip.py auto-continuum -i <cube.fits> [-p window sigma width distance exclusion iters smoothing]

Flags

Flag

Description

Default

-i / --input

Path to input FITS cube

(required)

-p / --params

Space-separated algorithm parameters (see below)

51 2.0 1 3 3 2 5

Parameters (in order)

Position

Name

Meaning

Default

1

window

Median-filter window size (channels)

51

2

sigma

Peak-detection threshold (× RMS)

2.0

3

width

Minimum peak width (channels)

1

4

distance

Minimum distance between peaks (channels)

3

5

exclusion

Channels to mask on each side of a detected peak

3

6

iters

Sigma-clipping iterations

2

7

smoothing

Spline smoothing factor

5

Algorithm

  1. Apply a median filter of width window as a first-pass continuum estimate.

  2. Detect emission peaks above sigma × RMS using scipy.signal.find_peaks.

  3. Mask exclusion channels on each side of every detected peak.

  4. Interpolate over masked regions, then re-apply the median filter.

  5. Iteratively sigma-clip outliers for iters passes.

  6. Fit a smoothing UnivariateSpline (k=3) to the cleaned continuum.

  7. Prompt for an output filename → save <name>.txt with columns Wavelength  Continuum_Fit.

Output file format

Tab-delimited two-column ASCII with a comment header:

# Type: fitted_continuum
# Wavelength  Continuum_Fit
3.0000e-06   1.2345e-02
3.0010e-06   1.2347e-02
...

The # Type: fitted_continuum line lets subtract-continuum — Subtract a continuum from a spectrum re-import the file later.

Examples

# Default parameters
python clip.py auto-continuum -i data/miri_cube.fits

# Custom parameters: larger window, tighter sigma, more exclusion
python clip.py auto-continuum -i data/miri_cube.fits -p 75 1.5 2 5 5 3 8

custom-continuum — Continuum from user-supplied points

Fits a Cubic Spline through a set of user-defined wavelength/flux anchor points and subtracts the result from the spectrum.

python clip.py custom-continuum -i <cube.fits> -p <points.csv>

Flags

Flag

Description

-i / --input

Path to input FITS cube

-p / --points

Path to CSV file containing anchor points

Points file format

Comma-separated, one point per line, no header:

3.5e-6,0.012
4.0e-6,0.015
4.8e-6,0.011

The spline is fit with bc_type='natural' and evaluated at every wavelength channel.

Output file format

# Wavelength  Original_Flux  Continuum_Fit  Subtracted_Result
3.0000e-06   1.4567e-02     1.2345e-02     2.2220e-03
...

Example

python clip.py custom-continuum -i data/muse_cube.fits -p my_points.csv

subtract-continuum — Subtract a continuum from a spectrum

Subtracts either a constant offset, a previously exported fitted-continuum file, or a raw-points file from the cube’s spectrum.

python clip.py subtract-continuum -i <cube.fits> -c <value_or_file>

Flags

Flag

Description

-i / --input

Path to input FITS cube

-c / --continuum

Numeric constant, path to a fitted-continuum .txt, or path to a raw-points .txt/.csv

Three modes — auto-detected from the ``-c`` argument

Mode

How detected

Behaviour

Constant

-c is a plain number (e.g. 0.05)

Subtracts the constant from every channel

Fitted continuum file

File contains a # Type: fitted_continuum header line

Interpolates the saved curve onto the current wavelength grid and subtracts

Raw points file

File has no recognised header

Parses comma-separated (wavelength, flux) pairs, fits a Cubic Spline, then subtracts

Output file format

# Wavelength  Original_Flux  Continuum_Fit  Subtracted_Result

A continuum exported by auto-continuum — Automatic continuum detection and export can be fed directly to subtract-continuum -c — the two commands are designed to pipe into each other.

Examples

# Constant baseline
python clip.py subtract-continuum -i data/alma_cube.fits -c 0.03

# Re-use a previously fitted continuum
python clip.py subtract-continuum -i data/alma_cube.fits -c continuum_export.txt

# Subtract using raw anchor points
python clip.py subtract-continuum -i data/nirspec_cube.fits -c my_baseline_points.csv

2d-rotate — Rotate a 2D FITS image

Rotates a 2D FITS image by an arbitrary angle and updates the WCS CD matrix so RA/Dec coordinates remain accurate after rotation.

python clip.py 2d-rotate -i <image.fits> -a <angle_degrees>

Flags

Flag

Description

-i / --input

Path to input 2D FITS file

-a / --angle

Rotation angle in degrees (positive = counter-clockwise)

What happens internally

  • scipy.ndimage.rotate with reshape=True and cval=NaN (empty border pixels are NaN, not zero).

  • The CD matrix is updated: CD_new = CD_orig × R⁻¹, where R is the 2D rotation matrix for -angle.

  • CRPIX is not changed — the reference pixel stays at the same sky coordinate.

Output

A new FITS file with the rotated image and an updated WCS header. The CLI prompts for the output filename.

Example

python clip.py 2d-rotate -i data/miri_intensity.fits -a 45
# Prompted: Enter filename to save ROTATED FITS: rotated_45deg
# → saves rotated_45deg.fits

2d-contour — Extract contour coordinates from a 2D FITS image

Generates contour lines at user-specified sigma levels, computes RA/Dec for every contour vertex using the image WCS, and saves the result as a text file.

python clip.py 2d-contour -i <image.fits> -l <level1> [level2 ...]

Flags

Flag

Description

-i / --input

Path to input 2D FITS file

-l / --levels

One or more sigma multipliers (space-separated)

Level definition

  • Background median and RMS are estimated with Astropy sigma_clipped_stats (3σ clipping).

  • Each level N draws a contour at median + N × RMS.

Output file format

Comma-separated ASCII with a comment header:

# IFU Analyzer 2D - Contour Export
# level, x_pixel, y_pixel, RA_deg, Dec_deg
3.000000e+00, 42.1234, 18.7654, 67.90591, 18.20682
...

Examples

# Single level
python clip.py 2d-contour -i data/moment0.fits -l 3

# Multiple levels
python clip.py 2d-contour -i data/moment0.fits -l 3 5 10 20

# High-significance contours only
python clip.py 2d-contour -i data/miri_intensity.fits -l 5 10 30 50

Output Formats — quick reference

Command

Output columns

auto-continuum

Wavelength  Continuum_Fit

custom-continuum

Wavelength  Original_Flux  Continuum_Fit  Subtracted_Result

subtract-continuum

Wavelength  Original_Flux  Continuum_Fit  Subtracted_Result

2d-rotate

FITS file with rotated image and updated WCS header

2d-contour

level, x_pixel, y_pixel, RA_deg, Dec_deg

Files exported by the CLI are fully compatible with the GUI’s subtract-continuum import — a continuum file exported by auto-continuum can be fed directly to subtract-continuum -c.
